intended_object: The invertible real-linear map ℂ → ℂ with 1 ↦ p − c and i ↦ q − c, for a nondegenerate triangle (c, p, q). It is the linear part of the affine map that carries the standard triangle onto conv{c, p, q}. This is read off the docstring, the module doc and the lemmas that follow it.
explanation:
The underlying linear map is `triangleLinearMap c p q`, defined as `Complex.basisOneI.constr ℝ ![p - c, q - c]`. It is the unique ℝ-linear map with 1 ↦ p − c and I ↦ q − c. The library proves that its determinant is `triangleDet c p q`. Under the hypothesis that this determinant is nonzero, `LinearMap.equivOfIsUnitDet` turns the map into a linear equivalence. Since ℂ is finite-dimensional over ℝ, it is then upgraded to a continuous linear equivalence. The lemmas that follow check that it has the intended values on 1 and I. They also show that it maps the standard triangle onto conv{c, p, q} and has determinant `triangleDet`. So the definition is exactly the triangle's coordinate map.

The construction is specific to the planar (ℂ ≅ ℝ²) setting of Green's theorem used in this development. It names one particular linear map rather than writing out a general Mathlib notion in a special case. The closest general Mathlib notions are `Basis.constr` and `LinearMap.equivOfIsUnitDet`, and the definition is built directly from them. So it is not too narrow.
